successors.text: Baol, the strip of land inland from the Petite Côte with Diourbel, Touba and Mbacké (the page gives no outline; the gazetteer's Diourbel region stands for it, the coast at Mbour and Saly is not drawn)

ledger.x: The Damel-Teigne union: Amary Ngoné Sobel Fall "became the first Damel-Teign, reigning over both kingdoms in a personal union".
1894: the kingdom ends; in 1895 its territory is divided into two provinces.

wars.name: Battle of Danki
wars.outcome: Baol and Cayor defeated the Emperor of Jolof and won independence.

wars.name: Lat Sukaabe Fall's conquest of Cayor
wars.outcome: "In 1697 Teigne Lat Sukaabe Fall conquered Cayor"; the cayor dossier's page gives 1693 for the same event.

wars.name: French conquest of Baol
wars.outcome: "The French conquest of Baol began in 1859"; most of the kingdom was conquered by 1874 and "complete control" only established in 1895.

certainty.note: Personal union with Cayor under the Damel-Teigne; no shape of its own here, the land is drawn in the cayor dossier.
The page gives towns and a general position but no outline; the 1549-1755 union with Cayor is drawn in the cayor dossier.
